name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 257 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 257 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: In Kashmir, authorities launched a terror-financing probe that led to searches of four locations, while a fire in Bemina destroyed 80 temporary shelters, killing two people. In Manipur, the chief minister warned armed groups that UAPA action will follow civilian violence and sought reports on groups linked to recent attacks, while the Supreme Court ordered the CBI to secure testimony from a third victim in a sexual-violence case. Amit Shah announced that Chhattisgarh is now naxal-free and poised for tourism growth. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: I Kashmir startet myndighetene en etterforskning av terrorfinansiering som førte til ransaking av fire lokasjoner, mens en brann i Bemina ødela 80 midlertidige leirer og drepte to personer. I Manipur advarte statsministeren væpnede grupper om at UAPA-tiltak vil følge sivil vold og ba om rapporter om grupper knyttet til nylige angrep, mens Høyesterett beordret CBI å sikre vitneforklaring fra et tredje offer i en sak om seksuell vold. Amit Shah kunngjorde at Chhattisgarh nå er naxalfritt og klar for vekst i turismen. UCDP registrerte 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
